newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: New black S.African oil company to be formed.
newsitem.headline: New black S.African oil company to be formed.

text.p: A group of South African black businessmen have reached an agreement to form a multi-million rand black-controlled oil company, Naledi Petroleum Ltd said on Monday.
The new company would be 77.5 percent owned by Naledi Petroleum Industries (NPI) and Sasol Oil (Pty) Ltd, a unit of Sasol Ltd, would have a 22.5 percent stake.
The company, which will be launched on June 1, plans to establish 40 service stations pumping in excess of an average of 275,000 litres of fuel per month over the next three years.
Eighteen of the service stations would be acquired from Sasol Oil and some would be built up from scratch, Sewela said.
"We regard the formation of Naledi Petroleum as a major step forward in terms of black economic empowerment in South Africa," NPI managing director Dominic Sewela told reporters.
He said the formation of the company was subject to certain conditions precedent including a due diligence investigation and funding.
He said the group would establish its first pump stations in Gauteng province, moving to other provinces later. They would also look into expanding to refineries in the future.
South African oil company and service station operator Zenex said earlier Monday that it was involved in talks on its sale to a black empowerment grouping.
Eric Molefi, the deputy chairman of NPI, said they were talking to Zenex but had not yet established any links with the company.
NPI has a broad-based shareholding structure which includes the South African National Civics Organisations and the National Hostel Residents Association.
